messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - smart-routing: canary variant health degraded -> sticky fallback loop detected. Paging @oncall-ml :rotating_light:
oncall-ml: Got it, joining. Seeing spike in 503s and a lot of traffic bouncing between region-us-west and eu-west.
sam: Confirmed, dashboards show canary-variant=v2-quant failing auth handshake, then policy routes to fallback variant v1 which is in eu-west, but sticky routing TTL causing repeated cross-region redirects.
tara: How long since rollout started?
sam: ~12m ago. Canary at 5% initially then 20% after automated ramp.
miguel: I'm seeing KV cache misses on the canary pods with error "incompatible-weights" logged during kernel init.
oncall-ml: Ok first steps: 1) Pause rollout 2) Set routing sticky TTL to 0 for affected routes 3) Force primary routing to dedicated-us-west for customer-facing endpoints while we investigate.
liz: I can pause the canary in the console now. Doing pause -> paused. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Deploy guard: canary rollout paused by liz.
oncall-ml: Sam/Tara, can one of you run a quick check to clear sticky sessions? Use: `rwctl routing clear-sticky --route /v1/generate --regions all`
sam: Running now... `clearing sticky sessions... done`
tara: I pushed a temporary routing override to prefer v1 in-us-west for 30m while we triage. Command: `rwctl routing set --route /v1/generate --policy prefer:v1 --duration 30m`
miguel: Looking at logs from the canary pods: model variant v2-quant fails when sequence init > 1024, fallback logic doesn't map variant compat correctly, ends up assigning incompatible runtime which crashes and marks instance unhealthy.
oncall-ml: That maps with the 'incompatible-weights' errors. Sounds like our compile/kernel selector picked a path incompatible with the quantized artifact. For mitigation, we should: A) keep canary paused B) ensure routing sticky cleared C) revert automated ramp and restore default routing policy.
sam: Reverting ramp and restoring default routing now. `rwctl rollout revert --canary-id 2026-03-10-42` -> success.
ops-bot: Routing override removed.
oncall-ml: cs-ops, can you assess customer impact? Which customers hit errors?
cs-ops: Pulling logs... approx 18 customer requests failed with 5xx in last 20m, mostly low-volume developer accounts and one mid-market customer (acme-retail) who reported latency + errors. Not seeing data exfiltration.
cs-ops: Noteworthy: ACME's requests were sticky to eu-west for a subset, causing higher latency but not data loss. They're flagged for outreach.
liz: Any need for a hotfix/rollback of the model variant artifact?
miguel: We'll need to repackage v2-quant with a safe kernel profile. Short term we shouldn't re-run the canary. I'll open an internal ticket.
oncall-ml: Handoff plan: I'm handing to sam for posttriage and follow-up. Sam, can you take lead and coordinate root cause and customer comms?
sam: Taking lead. I'll collect logs, create a postmortem draft, and coordinate with model-onboarding to fix kernel selection.
oncall-ml: Logging timeline and assigning oncall handoff. oncall-ml -> sam (handoff) at 1768005360.
ops-bot: Incident status updated to "mitigated" — sticky cleared, canary paused, routing restored.
cs-ops: I'll notify ACME support and offer a post-incident note.
ara: (reacts) :thumbsup:
liz: Quick note for the runbook: add a step to verify kernel compatibility before automated ramp to >10%. This would've stopped the ramp.
sam: Agreed, adding runbook entry now.
miguel: Ticket created: INF-9842 "kernel selector picks incompatible path for v2-quant" assigned to eng-ml with severity P2.
oncall-ml: Final checks: metrics back to baseline, error rate stable. Recommend we keep rollout paused until eng-ml confirms fixed artifact + verification tests.
sam: I'll set status page: private message to customers impacted and internal incident note.
cs-ops: Customer messages queued, small impact message drafted.
oncall-ml: Thanks team. Postmortem owner: sam. Action items: reproduce locally, fix packaging flow, add pre-ramp compatibility gate, improve sticky TTL default to 15s for canaries.
sam: Will post initial postmortem draft within 24h.
liz: Nice work.
ops-bot: Incident resolved. Closing paging loop."
